$comment: [[D-C-TAG-DEFINED-IN-A-PARAMETER-LIST-REFUSED]] runtime witness: a struct, union or enum DEFINED in a parameter list — in a definition, a prototype, a block-scope prototype, a function-pointer parameter's own list, and a type name inside a parameter's declarator. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-23: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 (WSL, -std=c2x and -std=c17), MinGW gcc (-std=c2x) and MSVC 19.51 (/std:clatest) all BUILD this file and RUN it to 42. Before `declHeadForParam` took the unified specifiers, DSS refused every one of these shapes with P_UnexpectedToken; and before the parameter-list stop in the tag float, the swap alone leaked a definition's tags and enumerators to the FILE scope (an enumerator of the list resolved in `main`, which all four references refuse).
$commentWhyNotVacuous: Each function computes with the type its own list defines — a member read through a pointer to it, a local of it named again in the body, an enumerator's value, a nested tag named in the body, a later parameter naming the earlier one's tag, and `sizeof` of a tag a parameter's declarator defines — and main subtracts the value each must return, so a wrong layout, a lost member or an enumerator bound to the wrong value moves the exit code. The prototype-only and block-scope-prototype shapes need only compile, and do.
$commentExpectWarnings: S_TagDeclaredInParameterList, one per tag the lists define (11), at the tag's name — or at the `struct` keyword for the anonymous one. ✔MEASURED: gcc 13.3.0 warns at exactly these 11 positions (its order puts Inner before Outer); clang 18.1.3 warns at the 10 named ones and not the anonymous struct; MSVC warns only C4116 on the anonymous one. The set is EXACT: a twelfth warning of this code, or a missing one, is a red.
